Thanks Marissa - useful recap and thanks for the recording. A few clarifying items from our side so we can confirm internally:

1) Latency: our target is p95 token latency <= 200ms for streaming responses (end-to-end from request to token emitted). p99 ideally < 400ms but we can discuss tradeoffs.
2) Throughput & concurrency: typical steady-state is ~50 concurrent users against the chat endpoint during support hours, with bursts up to ~300 concurrent during incident windows. Average prompt size ~120 tokens, expected response ~220 tokens.
3) Streaming: yes - we need token-by-token streaming to our web client for progressive render. Minimal buffering preferred.
4) SLA style questions: do you provide fallbacks to a lower-cost model during contention, and can we pin model version for consistency?

If you can confirm feasibility and share an estimated config for the benchmark (requested VM/GPU profile, model variant, expected token throughput), I can loop in our infra and procurement to lock times.

Alex - thanks for the clear targets. See inline below with our recommended configuration and next steps. I've attached a benchmark-config.yaml with parameters we use for the 48-hour run.

Summary response (quick):
- Latency: p95 token latency target <= 200ms - achievable in streaming mode with our recommended model and config; p99 < 400ms is realistic for steady-state but will depend on your peak concurrency and prompt distribution.
- Concurrency & burst: steady 50 conc / burst 300 - we recommend dedicated capacity for the POC or Reserved Dedicated lanes to ensure tail stability. For hosted run we can provision burst capacity but recommend a Dedicated eval for final sizing.
- Throughput: with avg prompt 120 tokens and response 220 tokens, estimate ~ (350 tokens/request). At 50 conc and avg think-time 6s, expected sustained throughput ~ 500 req/min. We'll model at 700 req/min to include headroom.
- Streaming: fully supported. We stream tokens as they are generated with <50ms server-side batching delay by default; end-to-end may add client network latency.
- Fallbacks & pinning: yes - we can configure routing policies to fallback to a smaller quantized variant on contention and allow model pinning for consistent output across runs.

Recommended benchmark config (high level):
- Model: redwood-extended-15B-quant (float16 hybrid)
- Hardware: 4x A100 (or equivalent) for the dedicated pool for the POC; single A100 for initial hosted run
- Batching: adaptive, target batch window 10ms for streaming
- KV cache warmup: 30 minutes prior to measurement window
- Measurement: 48-hour run, collect p50/p95/p99 token latencies, end-to-end response latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost estimates

Attachments: benchmark-config.yaml (includes our exact workload generator params).

Next steps / MAP items:
1) We schedule the benchmark kickoff - proposed Tue 2027-03-23 09:00 PT.
2) We exchange sample traces and a replay token for the workload (you provide).
3) Redwood runs 48-hour benchmark, shares results and recommended Dedicated sizing + MAP.
4) Procurement review & commit (if results align).

Can you confirm the proposed kickoff time and that procurement (Marta) is good to receive the benchmark results and draft MAP?

Thanks,
Marissa
